title: Phase Diagram and Critical Behaviour of the Two-Dimensional Potts Model with Long-Range Quenched Disorder
authors: Rodolfo Rocha, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, Marco Picco
abstract: We study the phase diagram and critical properties of the $q = 3$ and $q = 8$ Potts models with spatially correlated disorder governed by a power-law decay with exponent $a$. Building on the phase diagram proposed by Chippari et al. [3], where a transition from finite-disorder to infinite-disorder fixed points was identified as a function of a, we refine this picture by using wrapping probabilities of Fortuin-Kasteleyn clusters. Furthermore, using magnetic observables, we clarify the physical origin of the double-peak structure in the magnetic susceptibility and establish the validity of the hyper-scaling relation across all investigated regimes.
summary: This paper rigorously maps the phase diagram of the 2D Potts model under long-range, correlated quenched disorder. By analyzing the wrapping probability and magnetic susceptibility, the authors distinguish between different critical regimes, confirming the validity of hyperscaling relations across various disorder strengths. It provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how disorder influences phase transitions in lattice models.
main_problem: The study investigates the phase diagram and critical properties of the two-dimensional Potts model when subjected to long-range quenched disorder.
main_result: The work refines the phase diagram by distinguishing between regimes flowing to finite-disorder and infinite-disorder fixed points, confirming hyperscaling relations across different disorder strengths.
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques including computing the wrapping probability of Fortuin–Kasteleyn clusters and performing finite-size scaling analysis on magnetic observables.
model_or_system: The system is the $q$-state Potts model ($q=3, 8$) defined on a 2D lattice, with quenched bond disorder whose correlations decay via a power law $\langle J_i J_j angle \propto |x_i - x_j|^{-a}$.
key_observables: Wrapping probability $W(r, L)$, magnetic susceptibility $\chi(L,  eta)$, and magnetization density $\langle m angle(L,  eta)$.
important_parameters: Potts state number ($q$), disorder correlation exponent ($a$), disorder strength ratio ($r$), and system size ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the construction of correlated disorder via independent Ising model copies and assumes the critical point is analyzed at $ eta=1$ for certain sections.

Figures illustrate the dependence of the wrapping probability $W(r, L)$ on disorder strength $r$ for various exponents $a$, and show effective exponents $(\gamma/
u)_{	ext{eff}}(L)$ vs. $L$ to confirm scaling relations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the $q=3$ and $q=8$ cases, using the wrapping probability to map out the phase diagram, followed by a general confirmation of hyperscaling relations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the study of critical phenomena in disordered systems, especially the distinction between different types of fixed points (finite vs. infinite disorder), provides theoretical frameworks relevant to understanding glassy dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
